chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said: Some of our companions narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

People are two: one who relieves, and another who rests. As for the one who rests, it is the believer; when he dies, he rests from this world and its tribulation. As for the one who relieves, it is the disbeliever; when he dies, he relieves the trees, the animals, and many of the people.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the death of a believer and a disbeliever according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) presents a dialectical contrast between the internal spiritual state of the believer and the external social utility of the disbeliever. While the believer’s death signifies a transition to peace from the trials of dunya, the disbeliever’s death is portrayed as a physical relief for creation, highlighting the burden of their presence. This dual perspective underscores the Shia understanding of death not merely as an end, but as a transformative event with distinct metaphysical and worldly consequences.
